newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while calls ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower on feeder cattle, livestock analysts said.

Declining boxed beef values and expectations that packers may only pay $63 per cwt for fed cattle next week prompted the easier calls in live cattle futures. Although the current level of futures is a long-term support area, pressure is still likely as beef prices decline seasonally and heavy fed cattle supplies will continue to weigh on cash cattle for the next couple of months, analysts said.
However, some analysts cited active feedlot cattle sales this week which showed that feedlots are trying to stay current. This may lend some underlying support, they said.

Early indications ranged mixed on feeder cattle futures with some analysts looking for further support from declining grain prices, most notably easier corn futures indication. Feeder numbers will also be tight in the fall, they said.

However, others cited the decline in the CME feeder cattle index and current reduced demand for replacement cattle. Government reports indicated heavy cattle placements earlier in the year and the resulting larger number of cattle on feed nearing market-ready status this summer should reduce placements, they said
